themes_detail.label: Dead trees accelerating this week
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 4 THIS WEEK, up 540% from the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a potential widespread tree die-off or storm damage in Brownsville/Ocean Hill that warrants urgent environmental assessment.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 average weekly rate over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.94 indicates statistically significant spike
540% increase suggests acute event or seasonal stress rather than chronic undercare
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather (storms, drought, unseasonable heat/cold) killed trees across the district
Interview Parks Dept. about removal timelines and replanting plans for Brownsville green spaces

themes_detail.label: Garbage collection collapsing this week
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, up 273% from the 1.9 weekly average, indicating a sanitation services failure affecting residents across Brownsville/Ocean Hill.
evidence: 7 missed collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.76 indicates statistically significant spike
273% increase suggests a recent operational disruption (staff shortage, equipment failure, route change)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine what caused the collection failures this week—truck breakdowns, staffing issues, or scheduling changes
Canvass residential blocks to document uncollected refuse and estimate duration of service gap

themes_detail.label: Street signs vanishing rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints spiked to 3 two weeks ago (500% above the 0.5 weekly baseline), suggesting systematic theft, weather damage, or lack of maintenance affecting navigation and traffic safety in the district.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.0 indicates very high statistical significance
500% spike suggests concentrated incident or pattern rather than isolated reports
reporting_angles: Map the affected blocks and determine if signs were stolen, knocked down, or neglected by DOT
Interview residents and business owners about whether missing signs have disrupted traffic or created safety hazards

themes_detail.label: Cannabis retail complaints cluster
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints hit 7 two weeks ago, up 250% from the 2.0 weekly average, suggesting either an illegal dispensary operation surge or community concern about licensed retailers in Brownsville/Ocean Hill.
evidence: 7 cannabis retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.78 indicates statistically significant spike
250% increase suggests either new retail openings or uptick in complaint filings about existing operations
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with NYC Office of Cannabis Management license database to identify licensed vs. unlicensed retailers
Interview community members about whether complaints relate to illegal operations, odor, loitering, or other neighborhood impacts

themes_detail.label: Water leak complaints dropping sharply
themes_detail.summary: Water leak complaints fell to 7 THIS WEEK from a 25.6 weekly average, a 73% decline that could indicate either resolved infrastructure issues or potential under-reporting of a serious housing condition.
evidence: 7 water leak complaints THIS WEEK vs. 25.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of -3.8 indicates statistically significant downward deviation
73% drop is unusual and warrants investigation—either DEP resolved a major issue or residents stopped reporting
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine whether they completed major water main repairs or pipe replacements in Brownsville/Ocean Hill this week
Verify that the decline reflects actual infrastructure improvement, not under-reporting due to 311 system outage or community awareness gap
